title: How to hide cursor in Linear on Mac: alternative tools and keyboard-first workflow tips
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Linear on Mac: Solutions and Tips
description: Learn why you cannot hide cursor in Linear on Mac and discover the best system-wide utilities to hide your mouse pointer for presentations and recordings.
intro: There is no native feature within the Linear desktop app to hide your cursor because the interface is built for keyboard-first navigation. To hide your mouse pointer while working in Linear, you must use system-wide macOS utilities like Cursorcerer or built-in screen recording settings.
tldr: Linear does not support hiding the cursor internally.
The app is designed for keyboard-driven workflows, making the mouse optional.
Use third-party tools like Cursorcerer to hide the cursor system-wide.
Screen recording software often includes settings to hide the pointer during capture.
Mastering the command palette (⌘K) reduces your reliance on the mouse entirely.

blocks.text: Why Linear lacks a cursor hiding feature

Linear is a project management tool built for speed. Its core philosophy centers on keyboard interaction. The developers designed the interface so you can perform almost any action without touching your mouse. Because the mouse is secondary to the keyboard in their design language, they did not build a feature to hide the cursor within the app itself.

Many users confuse the Linear app with other software. Some look for cursor settings because they use the Cursor AI code editor, which integrates with Linear. Others search for this feature because they confuse the app name with LinearMouse, a utility for macOS mouse customization. Neither of these tools, nor the Linear app itself, provides a way to make the pointer invisible within the interface.
Managing your cursor for screen recordings

If you are trying to hide your cursor to create clean screen recordings of your Linear workflow, you should look at your recording software rather than the app. Professional tools like Screen Studio or even the native macOS Screen Capture tool offer options to hide the cursor.

items: Use Screen Studio: This app allows you to toggle cursor visibility with a single click during post-production.
Use QuickTime Player: When recording a portion of your screen, you can sometimes choose to hide the mouse in the recording settings.
Use Cursorcerer: This is a small, free utility for macOS. It allows you to hide your cursor using a global hotkey. It works across all applications, including Linear.

blocks.text: Since you cannot hide the cursor inside Linear, the best approach is to minimize its usage. Linear is faster when you keep your hands on the keyboard. Learning the core shortcuts makes the mouse feel unnecessary. The most important tool is the command palette.

Press ⌘K to open the command palette. From here, you can search for issues, switch views, or create new items. If you find yourself reaching for the mouse, stop and check the shortcut list. Press ? at any time to see the full list of available commands for your current view.
Common mistakes and how to fix them

A common mistake is assuming that setting the cursor to a pointer icon in Preferences changes its visibility. In Linear, go to Preferences > Interface and theme. You will see an option to opt for a pointer cursor when hovering over interactive elements. This only changes the icon style. It does not hide the cursor.

Another issue arises when shortcuts stop working. This usually happens because a text field is active. If your shortcuts like ⌘K or P are not triggering, press Esc to clear the active input. This returns focus to the main application layer where shortcuts are active.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor inside the Linear app?
faq.answer: No. Linear does not have a setting to hide the mouse cursor.

faq.question: Does LinearMouse help hide the cursor?
faq.answer: No. LinearMouse is a utility for customizing mouse behavior like scrolling and acceleration, not for hiding the cursor.

faq.question: How can I record my screen without the cursor?
faq.answer: Use a dedicated screen recording tool like Screen Studio or a system-wide utility like Cursorcerer to hide the pointer while you record.

requirements: Linear desktop app installed on macOS
Third-party utility like Cursorcerer if hiding the cursor is required

steps.name: Open Linear
steps.text: Launch the Linear desktop app from your Applications folder or via Spotlight.

steps.name: Use the Command Palette
steps.text: Press ⌘K to open the command menu. This is the primary way to navigate without a mouse.

steps.name: Avoid Mouse Usage
steps.text: Use the arrow keys to move between issues and Enter to select them. This keeps your hands on the keyboard.

steps.name: Install Cursorcerer for System-Wide Hiding
steps.text: Download and install Cursorcerer if you need to hide the cursor for presentations or recordings. It provides a global hotkey to toggle cursor visibility.

troubleshooting.fix: Press Esc to ensure no text field is currently focused.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find a hide cursor setting.
troubleshooting.fix: Linear does not have this feature. Use a third-party app like Cursorcerer.
